question: A 38-year-old woman comes to the physician because of a 1-month history of fatigue and pruritus. Examination of the abdomen shows an enlarged, nontender liver. Serum studies show an alkaline phosphatase level of 140 U/L, aspartate aminotransferase activity of 18 U/L, and alanine aminotransferase activity of 19 U/L. Serum antimitochondrial antibody titers are elevated. A biopsy specimen of this patient's liver is most likely to show which of the following findings?

options.opa: Fibrous, concentric obliteration of small and large bile ducts
options.opb: Intracytoplasmic eosinophilic inclusions in hepatocytes and cellular swelling
options.opc: Macrovesicular fatty infiltration and necrosis of hepatocytes
options.opd: Ballooning degeneration and apoptosis of hepatocytes
options.ope:
Lymphocytic infiltration of portal areas and periductal granulomas
"

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Elevated serum antimitochondrial antibody titers -> suggestive of primary biliary cholangitis -> 90% confidence. CHAIN: Primary biliary cholangitis -> characterized by autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts -> 85% confidence. CHAIN: Autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts -> fibrous, concentric obliteration of small and large bile ducts on liver biopsy -> 90%
enhanced_information: Elevated serum antimitochondrial antibody titers suggest primary biliary cholangitis, characterized by autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts. Liver biopsy is likely to show fibrous, concentric obliteration of small and large bile ducts.
analysis: The patient's presentation with fatigue, pruritus, elevated antimitochondrial antibody titers, and liver enzyme levels suggests primary biliary cholangitis, which is characterized by autoimmune destruction of intrahepatic bile ducts. The most likely finding on liver biopsy in this context is fibrous, concentric obliteration of small and large bile ducts.
